# U.S. Department of the Interior

> The Department of the Interior manages America's natural resources, public lands, energy policy, and trust responsibilities to Native Americans and Alaska Natives.

DOI is a cabinet-level federal agency overseeing diverse bureaus including the National Park Service, Bureau of Land Management, Bureau of Indian Affairs, and Bureau of Ocean Energy Management. The department balances conservation, resource management, and energy development while fulfilling trust obligations to Indigenous peoples.

## Key Topics

- National Park Service
- Bureau of Land Management
- Bureau of Indian Affairs
- Bureau of Ocean Energy Management
- American Indians and Alaska Natives
- Public lands management
- Energy policy
- Natural resources
- Water infrastructure
- Indigenous affairs
- Federal employment
- Trust funds administration
- National parks
- Conservation
- Heritage preservation

- [About Interior](https://www.doi.gov/about): DOI mission, organizational structure, and trust responsibilities overview
- [History of the Department of the Interior](https://www.doi.gov/about/history): Historical overview of DOI founding in 1849 and key events

- [Interior Leadership](https://www.doi.gov/interior-leadership): DOI leadership team and cabinet officials information

- [Departmental Offices](https://www.doi.gov/bureaus/offices): Directory of DOI departmental offices and organizational structure

- [Careers](https://www.doi.gov/careers): DOI careers page with federal job opportunities and application guide

## Specialized Programs & Initiatives

- [Bureau of Trust Funds Administration](https://www.doi.gov/ost): Trust funds administration for Indian trust assets and IIM accounts
- [Freedom 250](https://www.doi.gov/freedom250): DOI initiative highlighting historic sites and American heritage restoration
